content: An independent tuberculosis (TB) laboratory consultant for the Pan American Health Organization in Brazil, along with Francis Varaine from Médecins Sans Frontières in Paris, France, contributed to this work. The systematic review authors include Patrick Cudahy from Yale Medical Center, USA; Claudia M. Denkinger from FIND, Switzerland; Ruvandhi R. Nathavitharana from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, USA; Madhukar Pai from McGill University, Montreal, Canada; Samuel G. Schumacher from FIND, Switzerland; and Karen Steingart from the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, United Kingdom. Observers involved in the process were Sevim Ahmedov from USAID, USA; Emmanuelle Cambau from Groupe Hospitalier Lariboisière-Fernand Widal, France; David Dolinger from FIND, Switzerland; Miranda Langendam from the University of Amsterdam, Netherlands; Thomas Schön from Kalmar County Hospital and Linköping University, Sweden; and Belay Tessema from FIND, Switzerland. Acknowledgments are extended to the External Review Group, which included Heather Alexander from the CDC, USA; Martina Casenghi from Médecins Sans Frontières Access Campaign, Switzerland; Kathleen England from the KNCV Tuberculosis Foundation, Netherlands; Rumina Hasan from TB SRL Pakistan at Aga Khan University, Karachi, Pakistan; Nazir Ismail from TB SRL at the National Institute of Communicable Diseases, South Africa; Beatrice Lopez from Buenos Aires TB SRL, Argentina; Richard Lumb from Adelaide TB SRL, Australia; Satoshi Mitarai from the Japan Anti-Tuberculosis Association, Japan; Alaine Umubyeyi Nyaruhirira from Management Sciences for Health, South Africa; Rohit Sarin from the LRS Institute of TB and Respiratory Diseases, India; and Alena Shrahina from the National TB Programme, Belarus. Financial support for this work was provided by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and USAID through the USAID–WHO consolidated grant (grant number GHA-G-00–09–00003/US-2014–741). The funding sources had no influence on the development or content of these guidelines. The section on second-line line probe assays was prepared by Christopher Gilpin and Alexei Korobitsyn, with input from Karin Weyer, all of whom are part of the WHO Global TB Programme. This section was based on consensus reached during a Guideline Development Group (GDG) meeting convened by WHO in Montreux, Switzerland, on March 2, 2016. The WHO Steering Group overseeing this work included Christopher Gilpin, Alexei Korobitsyn, Fuad Mirzayev, Dennis Falzon, Matteo Zignol, and Karin Weyer, all from the WHO Global TB Programme. Members of the WHO GDG included Holger Schünemann (Chair and methodologist, McMaster University, Canada); Gavin Churchyard (Aurum Institute, South Africa); Daniela Maria Cirillo (HSR San Raffaele Scientific Institute/TB SRL, Italy); Chris Coulter (Queensland Mycobacterium Reference Laboratory, Australia); Greg Fox (University of Sydney, Australia); Moses Joloba (National Reference Laboratory of the National TB and Leprosy Programme, Uganda); James Posey (CDC, USA); Michael Rich (Partners in Health, USA); Leen Rigouts (Institute of Tropical Medicine, Belgium); Thomas M. Shinnick (independent consultant, USA); Rebecca Tadokera (Human Sciences Research Council, South Africa); Marie Alice Telles (independent TB laboratory consultant for the Pan American Health Organization, Brazil); and Francis Varaine (Médecins Sans Frontières, France). The systematic review team included Karen Steingart from the Cochrane Infectious Diseases Group at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, USA, and Grant Theron from Stellenbosch University, South Africa. The WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: rapid diagnostics for TB detection were developed with contributions from numerous experts and observers, including Sevim Ahmedov (USAID, USA), Emmanuelle Cambau (France), Miranda Langendam (Netherlands), Thomas Schön (Sweden), and Belay Tessema (Switzerland). External reviewers included Heather Alexander (CDC, USA), Martina Casenghi (Switzerland), Kathleen England (Netherlands), Rumina Hasan (Pakistan), Nazir Ismail (South Africa), Beatrice Lopez (Argentina), Richard Lumb (Australia), Satoshi Mitarai (Japan), Alaine Umubyeyi Nyaruhirira (South Africa), Rohit Sarin (India), and Alena Shrahina (Belarus). The guidelines were drafted by Alexei Korobitsyn with input from Annabel Baddeley, Christopher Gilpin, and Lara Vojnov, based on consensus achieved at the GDG meeting held from May 14–16, 2019. Technical editing was provided by Hilary Cadman and her team at Cadman Editing Services, Australia. Funding for this work was provided by USAID through the USAID–WHO consolidated grant (grant number US-2016–0961). The views of the funding agency did not influence the development or content of these guidelines. The WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: rapid diagnostics for TB detection also include recommendations on nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) for detecting TB and drug-resistant TB. The Guideline Development Group for this section was co-chaired by Holger Schünemann (McMaster University, Canada) and Jeremiah Chakaya Muhwa (International Union Against TB and Lung Diseases, Kenya). Other members included Denise Arakaki-Sanchez (Ministry of Health, Brazil), David Branigan (Treatment Action Group, USA), Daniela Cirillo (San Raffaele Supranational TB Reference Laboratory, Italy), Celina Anna Maria Garfin (National TB Programme, Philippines), Petra de Haas (KNCV Tuberculosis Foundation, Netherlands), Patricia Hall (CDC, USA), Rumina Hasan (Aga Khan University, Pakistan), Xia Hui (China CDC, China), Farzana Ismail (South Africa), Katharina Kranzer (London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, Zimbabwe), Blessina Kumar (Global Coalition of TB Activists, India), Nagalingeswaran Kumarasamy (YRG CARE, India), Lindiwe Mvusi (South Africa), Viet Nhung Nguyen (Vietnam), Mark Nicol (Australia), Leen Rigouts (Belgium), Thomas Shinnick (USA), Hojoon Sohn (USA), Sabira Tahseen (Pakistan), Ezio Tavora dos Santos Filho (Brazil), Carrie Tudor (South Africa), Diana Vakhrusheva (Russia), and Elisabetta Walters (South Africa). The systematic review team included Mika Kohli (McGill University, Canada), Samuel Schumacher (FIND, Switzerland), Karen Steingart (USA), and Alice Zwerling (University of Ottawa, Canada). Additional technical expertise was provided by Nim Arinaminpathy (Imperial College London, UK), Claudia Denkinger (Germany), Nora Engel (Netherlands), Helena Huerga (Belgium), Emmanuel Moreau (Switzerland), Krishna Reddy (USA), Saskia Ricks (UK), Samuel Schumacher (Switzerland), and Rita Szekely (Switzerland). Observers included Patricia Hall (CDC, USA), Karen Heichman (Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, USA), and Wayne van Gemert (Stop TB Partnership, Switzerland). The WHO Steering Committee overseeing this work included Nazir Ismail, Alexei Korobitsyn, Dennis Falzon, Cecily Miller, Fuad Mirzayev, Lice Gonzalez-Angulo, Anna Dean, Annabel Baddeley, Carl-Michael Nathanson, Lara Vojnov, Mercedes Gonzalez, and Soudeh Ehsani. Funding for this work was provided by the Russian Federation through the Russian Federation–WHO consolidated grant (grant number REM-RUS-030). The views of the funding agency did not influence the development or content of these guidelines. Technical editing was provided by Cadman Editing Services, and design was managed by Inis Communication. This version maintains the original content's integrity while presenting it in a clear, professional, and structured manner.
